name: Boutique hotel
summary: Independent or lifestyle/soft-brand hotel (~50–200 keys), usually urban and often an adaptive reuse, with design-forward finishes and a destination restaurant/bar or rooftop. No survey reports boutique hotels as a category, so the default is derived between HVS select-service and full-service per-key costs and RLB metro 3–5 star $/SF; HVS "redevelopment projects" medians anchor the adaptive-reuse case. Treat as a derived estimate.

typicalSize.method: Boutique/lifestyle hotels are typically smaller than full-service; 50–200 keys with 120 as a judgment mid.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Net guestrooms ~350–470 SF (HCEG midscale to upper upscale, e18) plus bath ≈ 420–540 SF; F&B/bar/lobby lounge add ~80–200 SF/key but meeting space is limited; adaptive reuse buildings are less efficient. ~600–950 GSF/key, mid 750.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Urban infill mid-rise; 120 keys on ~0.5–1.5 acre.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Urban boutiques frequently rely on valet/shared garages (0–0.5); suburban/resort-town boutiques ~1.0. Local code governs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Bracketed by HVS 2025-data building & site improvements: select-service average $156,219 (e1) and full-service median $305,266 (e2); HVS redevelopment projects (existing-building conversions) median $193,644 / avg $287,189 in 2023 data (e4) and $196,077 median in 2021–22 data (e5). Midpoint of select-service average and full-service median = $231k; x0.91 (HVS includes permits/engineering/contingency) → $210k; plus ~20–25% for design-forward finishes and a destination F&B program → ~$260k. RLB 2026 metro check: midpoint of 3-star median-high ($475/SF) and 5-star median-low ($483/SF) ≈ $480/SF (e6, e7) x 750 SF ≈ $360k in large metros, consistent with the mid after a national discount. Low $180k ≈ 0.91 x 2023 redevelopment median ($194k → $176k); high $420k ≈ RLB 5-star metro median-low ($483) x ~870 SF.

perSF.method: Mid = $260k ÷ 750 SF ≈ $347/SF. Low ≈ RSMeans national 15-story hotel ~$262/SF (e8); high between RLB metro 3-star median-high ($475) and 5-star median midpoint ($613) (e6, e7).

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC and OH&P, limited urban on-site work; for adaptive reuse the figure covers demolition, structural/MEP upgrades and new interiors (not acquisition). Excludes land/building acquisition, FF&E/OS&E, kitchen equipment, soft costs, pre-opening, permits, contingency, off-sites, impact/tap fees, financing.

qualityTiers.method: Economy = low/mid (0.69, a micro/pod-style boutique); premium ≈ high/mid trimmed (1.6 → 1.35); luxury reflects small luxury hotels approaching full luxury per-key costs (1.8).

systemSplit.method: Derived from the full-service split with: finishes (09) raised to 15% and casework/millwork (12) to 3% for design-forward interiors; existing conditions/selective demolition (02) 2% for typical partial adaptive reuse; sitework (31–33) reduced to 4% for urban infill.

lineItems.name: Pre-opening, OS&E, launch marketing and working capital

cost.method: Between HVS 2025-data select-service ($3,561 median / $5,477 avg, e15) and full-service ($11,842 / $14,075, e14); independents carry extra launch marketing and F&B pre-opening without brand support, so the mid sits near full-service.

lineItems.notes: Owner cost: OS&E (custom-branded), F&B opening inventory, pre-opening payroll and marketing, operating reserves.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Between HVS full-service FF&E ($36,752 median / $43,928 avg, 2025 data, e9) and luxury ($94,613–$138,317 medians, e11, e10); smaller boutiques with limited meeting space need less public-area FF&E than full-service, so mid ≈ full-service median.

pctOfHard.method: HVS soft ÷ building (2025-data medians): select-service 16.5% (e13), full-service 22.6% (e12). Boutiques carry custom architecture and interior design (HCEG: design, PM and procurement ~10% of a renovation budget, e19), historic/adaptive-reuse consultants and F&B concept design, so mid 20% (excl. financing) with a higher high.

softCosts.notes: Includes custom interior design and procurement agent, F&B concept/kitchen design, branding, historic tax-credit consultants where applicable, soft-brand application/technical fees if affiliated.

design.method: Custom design with no prototype; higher design contingency.

hard.method: Adaptive reuse / existing-building unknowns push hard contingency above new prototype hotels; use the low end for ground-up.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard $180k–$420k + soft 16–28% + FF&E $25k–$55k → ~$235k–$595k; bracketed by HVS all-in less land for select-service (~$183k–$217k, e16) and full-service (~$437k–$526k, e17), widened up for urban luxury boutiques.

openQuestions: No direct boutique-hotel cost source found (search budget exhausted); a public budget for a boutique/adaptive-reuse hotel (e.g., a historic tax credit application or TIF packet) would make this sourced.
Adaptive-reuse vs. ground-up boutiques could be split; existing-building acquisition is excluded here.
